notes: General category has one primary observance for every calendar day. Dates and origin facts are best-effort and SHOULD be verified against a canonical source before shipping. `date` = fixed month/day. `rule` = floating (nth weekday of a month). Exactly one of `date` or `rule` must be present. Feb 29 entries only appear in leap years.

observances.title: New Year's Day
observances.blurb: The first day of the Gregorian calendar year, and a public holiday across most of the world.

observances.title: National Science Fiction Day
observances.blurb: A day to go somewhere impossible without getting off the couch.

observances.title: National Chocolate-Covered Cherry Day
observances.blurb: A minor food holiday for the cordial cherry, a candy dating to the early 1900s.

observances.title: National Spaghetti Day
observances.blurb: A day for one of the most common pasta shapes, a staple of Italian-American cooking.

observances.title: National Bird Day
observances.blurb: Focuses on the welfare of birds, both wild and captive. It coincides with the end of the Christmas Bird Count.

observances.title: National Bean Day
observances.blurb: Marks the January 6 death of Gregor Mendel, who studied heredity using pea plants.

observances.title: National Tempura Day
observances.blurb: A day for the Japanese method of light battering and frying, itself adapted from 16th-century Portuguese cooking.

observances.title: National Bubble Bath Day
observances.blurb: A small self-care observance in the depths of winter. Take the long bath.

observances.title: National Apricot Day
observances.blurb: A day for the stone fruit, grown for thousands of years across Central and West Asia.

observances.title: National Bittersweet Chocolate Day
observances.blurb: Recognizes dark chocolate with a high cocoa content and little added sugar.

observances.title: National Milk Day
observances.blurb: Marks January 11, 1878, often cited as the first day milk was delivered in glass bottles in the U.S.

observances.title: National Curried Chicken Day
observances.blurb: A day for chicken curry, a dish with countless regional versions across South and Southeast Asia.

observances.title: National Rubber Ducky Day
observances.blurb: Tied to Ernie's song on Sesame Street; the character's rubber duck was given the birthday January 13.

observances.title: National Dress Up Your Pet Day
observances.blurb: Started in 2009 by a pet lifestyle expert to promote adoption. The dog may not share your enthusiasm.

observances.title: National Hat Day
observances.blurb: A light observance of headwear of all kinds, from ball caps to berets.

observances.title: Martin Luther King Jr. Day
observances.blurb: A federal holiday on the third Monday in January honoring the civil rights leader, born January 15, 1929. Widely observed as a day of service.

observances.title: National Nothing Day
observances.blurb: Proposed by a journalist in 1972 as a day to just be, without celebrating anything.

observances.title: National Hot Buttered Rum Day
observances.blurb: Rum, butter, brown sugar, and warm spices. A colonial-era answer to a cold January.

observances.title: Ditch New Year's Resolutions Day
observances.blurb: Roughly the point in January when most resolutions quietly expire. This one makes it official.

observances.title: National Bagel and Lox Day
observances.blurb: Cured salmon, cream cheese, capers, red onion, on a good bagel. A deli classic.

observances.title: Winnie the Pooh Day
observances.blurb: Celebrates the January 18 birthday of author A. A. Milne, born 1882.

observances.title: National Popcorn Day
observances.blurb: A day for one of the oldest snack foods; corn kernels that pop have been found at archaeological sites thousands of years old.

observances.title: National Cheese Lover's Day
observances.blurb: A broad food holiday for cheese in all its forms.

observances.title: National Hugging Day
observances.blurb: Created in 1986 to encourage people to show affection openly.

observances.title: National Blondie Day
observances.blurb: A day for the blondie, a bar cookie made with brown sugar and vanilla instead of cocoa.

observances.title: National Pie Day
observances.blurb: Established by the American Pie Council; distinct from March 14's Pi Day.

observances.title: National Peanut Butter Day
observances.blurb: A day for the spread; a version was patented in the U.S. in the late 1800s.

observances.title: National Opposite Day
observances.blurb: A children's game of saying the reverse of what you mean, adopted as an informal holiday.

observances.title: National Spouses Day
observances.blurb: A day to recognize a husband or wife, separate from Valentine's Day and anniversaries.

observances.title: National Chocolate Cake Day
observances.blurb: A food holiday for chocolate cake, which became common after cocoa powder was mass-produced in the 1800s.

observances.title: National Kazoo Day
observances.blurb: Honors the kazoo, a simple membrane instrument patented in the U.S. in 1883.

observances.title: National Puzzle Day
observances.blurb: Covers jigsaw puzzles, crosswords, and logic puzzles alike.

observances.title: National Croissant Day
observances.blurb: A day for the laminated pastry, popularized in France from an earlier Austrian shape.

observances.title: National Hot Chocolate Day
observances.blurb: A midwinter food holiday for the drink, consumed in Mesoamerica long before it reached Europe.

observances.title: National Hangover Day
observances.blurb: An informal January 1 observance that follows directly from New Year's Eve.

observances.title: National Clean Off Your Desk Day
observances.blurb: Observed the second Monday in January, near the start of the working year.

observances.title: National Freedom Day
observances.blurb: Marks February 1, 1865, when Abraham Lincoln signed the resolution that became the 13th Amendment.

observances.title: Groundhog Day
observances.blurb: A tradition from Pennsylvania Dutch folklore; a groundhog's emergence is said to predict the length of winter.

observances.title: National Carrot Cake Day
observances.blurb: A day for the spiced cake; using carrots as a sweetener dates back to medieval Europe.

observances.title: National Homemade Soup Day
observances.blurb: A winter food holiday encouraging cooking from scratch.

observances.title: National Weatherperson's Day
observances.blurb: For the forecasters standing in front of a green screen, right about 40% of the time.

observances.title: National Frozen Yogurt Day
observances.blurb: A day for the dessert, which saw major popularity in the U.S. in the 1980s.

observances.title: Send a Card to a Friend Day
observances.blurb: An informal prompt to mail a physical card to someone.

observances.title: Boy Scouts Day
observances.blurb: Marks the February 8, 1910 founding of the Boy Scouts of America.

observances.title: National Pizza Day
observances.blurb: A day for one of America's most popular foods, brought by Italian immigrants in the late 1800s.

observances.title: National Umbrella Day
observances.blurb: A day for an object used for shade and rain for over a thousand years.

observances.title: National Make a Friend Day
observances.blurb: An informal nudge to introduce yourself to someone new.

observances.title: National Plum Pudding Day
observances.blurb: A day for the dense steamed dessert, which despite the name usually contains raisins rather than plums.

observances.title: National Tortellini Day
observances.blurb: A day for the ring-shaped stuffed pasta from the Emilia region of Italy.

observances.title: Valentine's Day
observances.blurb: A day associated with romantic love since the Middle Ages, named for one or more early Christian martyrs called Valentine.

observances.title: National Gumdrop Day
observances.blurb: A day for the firm, sugar-coated candy common in the U.S. since the 1800s.

observances.title: National Almond Day
observances.blurb: A day for the almond, a tree nut grown heavily in California, which supplies most of the world's supply.

observances.title: Random Acts of Kindness Day
observances.blurb: Promotes small unprompted acts of generosity; observed more widely since the late 1990s.

observances.title: Presidents' Day
observances.blurb: A federal holiday on the third Monday in February, originally honoring George Washington's birthday.

observances.title: National Battery Day
observances.blurb: Never the size you need, and always dead in the one remote you actually use.

observances.title: National Chocolate Mint Day
observances.blurb: A day for the pairing of chocolate and mint, common in candies and after-dinner sweets.

observances.title: National Love Your Pet Day
observances.blurb: A day to give extra attention to companion animals.

observances.title: National Sticky Bun Day
observances.blurb: A day for the caramel-and-nut roll, related to German Schnecken brought by immigrants to Pennsylvania.

observances.title: National Margarita Day
observances.blurb: A day for the tequila-and-lime cocktail, popularized in the U.S. from the 1940s onward.

observances.title: National Banana Bread Day
observances.blurb: A day for the quick bread, which became popular after baking soda and powder reached home kitchens.

observances.title: National Tortilla Chip Day
observances.blurb: A day for the fried or baked corn chip, commercialized in Los Angeles in the mid-20th century.

observances.title: National Clam Chowder Day
observances.blurb: A day for the New England soup; the Manhattan tomato version remains a regional dispute.

observances.title: National Pistachio Day
observances.blurb: A day for the pistachio, one of the oldest cultivated nuts, native to Western Asia.

observances.title: National Strawberry Day
observances.blurb: A day for the strawberry; the modern large-fruited variety was bred in 18th-century Europe.

observances.title: National Tooth Fairy Day
observances.blurb: Recognizes the folk tradition of leaving a coin for a child's lost baby tooth.

observances.title: Leap Day
observances.blurb: The extra day added to February every four years to keep the calendar aligned with the solar year.

observances.title: Singles Awareness Day
observances.blurb: An informal February 15 counter-observance to Valentine's Day.

observances.title: National Peanut Butter Lover's Day
observances.blurb: A day for enthusiasts of peanut butter, distinct from January's broader observance.

observances.title: National Old Stuff Day
observances.blurb: An informal prompt to reconsider routines and habits you've never questioned.

observances.title: National Mulled Wine Day
observances.blurb: A day for wine warmed with spices, a winter drink across Europe for centuries.

observances.title: National Pound Cake Day
observances.blurb: A day for the cake named after its original recipe: a pound each of butter, sugar, eggs, and flour.

observances.title: National Cheese Doodle Day
observances.blurb: A day for the puffed corn snack, produced commercially in the U.S. from the mid-20th century.

observances.title: National Oreo Day
observances.blurb: Marks the date the first Oreo was sold in 1912.

observances.title: National Cereal Day
observances.blurb: A day for breakfast cereal, an industry that grew out of 19th-century American health movements.

observances.title: International Women's Day
observances.blurb: A global day marking women's rights and achievements, observed since the early 1900s and recognized by the UN.

observances.title: National Meatball Day
observances.blurb: A day for the seasoned ground-meat ball, found in cuisines worldwide.

observances.title: National Ranch Dressing Day
observances.blurb: A day for ranch dressing, invented at a California dude ranch in the 1950s and now the top-selling U.S. dressing.

observances.title: National Napping Day
observances.blurb: Placed the day after the switch to daylight saving time, when many people lose an hour of sleep.

observances.title: National Baked Scallops Day
observances.blurb: A day for the shellfish, prepared here baked with butter and breadcrumbs.

observances.title: National Good Samaritan Day
observances.blurb: Encourages helping strangers, named for the parable in the Gospel of Luke.

observances.title: Pi Day
observances.blurb: Celebrates the constant pi (3.14) on 3/14. Bakeries and math teachers both lean in hard.

observances.title: National Poire Belle Hélène Day
observances.blurb: A day for the French dessert of poached pears with chocolate sauce, created in the 1860s.

observances.title: National Panda Day
observances.blurb: Raises awareness of the giant panda, a conservation-reliant species native to south-central China.

observances.title: St. Patrick's Day
observances.blurb: A cultural and religious holiday marking the patron saint of Ireland; widely celebrated across the Irish diaspora.

observances.title: National Sloppy Joe Day
observances.blurb: A day for the loose ground-beef sandwich, a U.S. lunchroom staple since at least the 1930s.

observances.title: National Poultry Day
observances.blurb: A day for domesticated birds raised for meat and eggs.

observances.title: International Day of Happiness
observances.blurb: A UN observance, begun in 2013, recognizing well-being as a goal of public policy.

observances.title: World Poetry Day
observances.blurb: A UNESCO observance, adopted in 1999, supporting poetry and linguistic diversity.

observances.title: World Water Day
observances.blurb: A UN observance since 1993 focused on fresh water and access to safe drinking water.

observances.title: National Puppy Day
observances.blurb: Created in 2006 to celebrate puppies and promote adoption from shelters.

observances.title: National Cheesesteak Day
observances.blurb: A day for the Philadelphia sandwich of thin-sliced beef and melted cheese, dating to the 1930s.

observances.title: International Waffle Day
observances.blurb: From the Swedish Våffeldagen, which arose from confusion with a church feast day of similar name.

observances.title: National Spinach Day
observances.blurb: A day for the leafy green, native to Persia and cultivated for well over a thousand years.

observances.title: National Spanish Paella Day
observances.blurb: A day for the rice dish from Valencia, traditionally cooked over an open fire in a wide shallow pan.

observances.title: Something on a Stick Day
observances.blurb: An informal food holiday for anything served on a skewer or stick.

observances.title: National Lemon Chiffon Cake Day
observances.blurb: A day for chiffon cake, an American invention from the 1920s that uses oil for a light crumb.

observances.title: National Pencil Day
observances.blurb: Marks March 30, 1858, when Hymen Lipman patented a pencil with an attached eraser.

observances.title: National Crayon Day
observances.blurb: A day for wax crayons; Crayola sold its first eight-color box in 1903.

observances.title: April Fools' Day
observances.blurb: A long-standing tradition of hoaxes and practical jokes on April 1, recorded in Europe since at least the 1500s.

observances.title: National Peanut Butter and Jelly Day
observances.blurb: A day for the sandwich, which spread widely in the U.S. after both spreads became cheap and shelf-stable.

observances.title: National Chocolate Mousse Day
observances.blurb: A day for the aerated French dessert; 'mousse' is French for foam.

observances.title: National Vitamin C Day
observances.blurb: The reason sailors packed limes, and a fair excuse to drink orange juice at any hour.

observances.title: National Caramel Day
observances.blurb: A day for caramel, made by heating sugar until it browns and develops a nutty flavor.

observances.title: National Caramel Popcorn Day
observances.blurb: A day for popcorn coated in caramel; commercial versions date to the 1890s.

observances.title: World Health Day
observances.blurb: Marks the founding of the World Health Organization in 1948; each year highlights a specific health theme.

observances.title: National Empanada Day
observances.blurb: A day for the stuffed, folded pastry found across Spain, Latin America, and the Philippines.

observances.title: National Chinese Almond Cookie Day
observances.blurb: A day for the crumbly cookie served in Chinese-American restaurants, often around the Lunar New Year.

observances.title: National Siblings Day
observances.blurb: For the people who knew you before you had a personality.

observances.title: National Cheese Fondue Day
observances.blurb: A day for the Swiss dish of melted cheese; it was heavily promoted as a national dish in the 1930s.

observances.title: National Grilled Cheese Day
observances.blurb: A day for the sandwich, which became a U.S. staple during the 1920s with sliced bread and processed cheese.

observances.title: National Peach Cobbler Day
observances.blurb: A day for the baked fruit dessert developed by early American settlers without proper pie equipment.

observances.title: National Dolphin Day
observances.blurb: Raises awareness of dolphins, among the most intelligent marine mammals.

observances.title: National That Sucks Day
observances.blurb: An informal observance placed on the U.S. tax filing deadline, for airing minor frustrations.

observances.title: National Wear Your Pajamas to Work Day
observances.blurb: An informal, lighthearted observance; for remote workers it may not require any effort.

observances.title: National Cheese Ball Day
observances.blurb: A day for the molded cream-cheese appetizer, a fixture of American parties since the mid-1900s.

observances.title: National Animal Crackers Day
observances.blurb: A day for the boxed cookie; the familiar circus-wagon package appeared in the U.S. in 1902.

observances.title: National Garlic Day
observances.blurb: A day for garlic, used as food and folk medicine for thousands of years.

observances.title: National Pineapple Upside-Down Cake Day
observances.blurb: A day for the cake, which spread in the 1920s after canned sliced pineapple became widely available.

observances.title: National Tea Day
observances.blurb: A day for tea, the world's most consumed drink after water.

observances.title: Earth Day
observances.blurb: First held in 1970, now observed in nearly 200 countries as a focus for environmental action.

observances.title: National Picnic Day
observances.blurb: A day for outdoor meals, a leisure tradition that grew in the 19th century.

observances.title: National Pigs in a Blanket Day
observances.blurb: A day for sausages wrapped in dough or pastry, a common party appetizer.

observances.title: National Telephone Day
observances.blurb: Marks the era of Alexander Graham Bell's 1876 telephone patent.

observances.title: National Pretzel Day
observances.blurb: A day for the pretzel, whose knot shape is often traced to European monasteries around the 7th century.

observances.title: National Prime Rib Day
observances.blurb: A day for the standing rib roast, a traditional centerpiece cut of beef.

observances.title: National Superhero Day
observances.blurb: Started by Marvel employees in 1995 to honor both fictional heroes and real-life ones.

observances.title: National Shrimp Scampi Day
observances.blurb: A day for the Italian-American dish of shrimp in garlic butter and white wine.

observances.title: National Raisin Day
observances.blurb: A day for dried grapes; California's raisin industry began after an 1870s heat wave dried a grape crop on the vine.

observances.title: Tell a Story Day
observances.blurb: An informal observance encouraging oral storytelling, observed on different dates in the US and UK.

observances.title: May Day
observances.blurb: A spring festival with roots in pre-Christian Europe, marked by flowers, dancing, and in many countries labor marches.

observances.title: National Truffle Day
observances.blurb: A day for the edible underground fungus, foraged with trained dogs or pigs and sold by weight of gold.

observances.title: National Chocolate Custard Day
observances.blurb: A day for the egg-thickened chocolate dessert.

observances.title: Star Wars Day
observances.blurb: An unofficial fan holiday built on the pun 'May the Fourth be with you.'

observances.title: Cinco de Mayo
observances.blurb: Marks Mexico's 1862 victory at the Battle of Puebla. It is a bigger celebration in the U.S. than in most of Mexico.

observances.title: National Beverage Day
observances.blurb: A broad, informal day for drinks of all kinds.

observances.title: National Roast Leg of Lamb Day
observances.blurb: A day for the roast, a traditional dish for Easter and other spring feasts in many cultures.

observances.title: National Coconut Cream Pie Day
observances.blurb: A day for the custard pie topped with whipped cream and toasted coconut.

observances.title: Lost Sock Memorial Day
observances.blurb: An informal, tongue-in-cheek observance for socks that vanish in the laundry.

observances.title: National Clean Up Your Room Day
observances.blurb: An informal prompt to tidy a space you've been avoiding.

observances.title: National Eat What You Want Day
observances.blurb: An informal day to set aside dietary rules for a single meal.

observances.title: National Nutty Fudge Day
observances.blurb: A day for fudge with nuts; the candy is often linked to women's colleges in the 1880s and 90s.

observances.title: National Apple Pie Day
observances.blurb: A day for the pie, brought to America by European settlers and long used as a symbol of the country.

observances.title: National Buttermilk Biscuit Day
observances.blurb: A day for the quick bread central to Southern U.S. cooking.

observances.title: National Chocolate Chip Day
observances.blurb: A day for the baking chip, created after the chocolate chip cookie's invention in the 1930s.

observances.title: National Barbecue Day
observances.blurb: A day for slow cooking meat over wood or charcoal, with distinct regional traditions across the U.S.

observances.title: National Walnut Day
observances.blurb: A day for the walnut, one of the oldest tree foods known to humans.

observances.title: National No Dirty Dishes Day
observances.blurb: An informal day to skip cooking, and the cleanup that follows.

observances.title: National Devil's Food Cake Day
observances.blurb: A day for the rich chocolate cake; the name contrasts it with the pale, light angel food cake.

observances.title: National Quiche Lorraine Day
observances.blurb: A day for the savory custard tart from the Lorraine region of France, made with bacon or lardons.

observances.title: National Strawberries and Cream Day
observances.blurb: A day for the pairing, famously associated with the Wimbledon tennis championships.

observances.title: National Maritime Day
observances.blurb: A U.S. observance honoring the merchant marine, marked on the 1819 departure date of the first steamship to cross the Atlantic.

observances.title: National Taffy Day
observances.blurb: A day for the chewy pulled candy, closely tied to American seaside boardwalks.

observances.title: National Scavenger Hunt Day
observances.blurb: A day for the game, popularized as a party activity by columnist Elsa Maxwell in the 1930s.

observances.title: National Wine Day
observances.blurb: A day for wine, produced from fermented grapes for at least 8,000 years.

observances.title: Memorial Day
observances.blurb: A U.S. federal holiday on the last Monday in May honoring those who died in military service. It grew out of post-Civil War remembrance days.

observances.title: National Blueberry Cheesecake Day
observances.blurb: A day for cheesecake topped with blueberry compote.

observances.title: National Grape Popsicle Day
observances.blurb: A day for the frozen treat; the popsicle was reportedly invented by an 11-year-old in 1905.

observances.title: National Hamburger Day
observances.blurb: A day for the ground-beef sandwich, which spread nationwide after the 1904 St. Louis World's Fair.

observances.title: National Biscuit Day
observances.blurb: A UK observance for the biscuit, which Americans would call a cookie.

observances.title: National Water a Flower Day
observances.blurb: An informal reminder to tend to houseplants and gardens.

observances.title: National Smile Day
observances.blurb: An informal observance encouraging small gestures of friendliness.

observances.title: Mother's Day
observances.blurb: Honors mothers and motherhood; the U.S. version, on the second Sunday in May, was founded by Anna Jarvis in 1908.

observances.title: National Say Something Nice Day
observances.blurb: An informal prompt to offer a genuine compliment out loud.

observances.title: National Rocky Road Day
observances.blurb: A day for the ice cream flavor of chocolate, nuts, and marshmallows, named during the Great Depression.

observances.title: National Egg Day
observances.blurb: A day for the egg, one of the most widely used ingredients in cooking and baking.

observances.title: National Cheese Day
observances.blurb: A day for cheese, of which there are well over a thousand recognized varieties.

observances.title: World Environment Day
observances.blurb: The UN's main day for environmental awareness, held since 1973 with a different host country each year.

observances.title: National Yo-Yo Day
observances.blurb: It's all in the wrist, plus roughly two years of practice.

observances.title: National Chocolate Ice Cream Day
observances.blurb: A day for the flavor, which predates vanilla ice cream in Europe.

observances.title: Best Friends Day
observances.blurb: An informal day to acknowledge a close friendship.

observances.title: National Strawberry Rhubarb Pie Day
observances.blurb: A day for the early-summer pie balancing sweet strawberries with tart rhubarb stalks.

observances.title: National Iced Tea Day
observances.blurb: A day for chilled tea, popularized in the U.S. at the 1904 St. Louis World's Fair.

observances.title: National Corn on the Cob Day
observances.blurb: A day for sweet corn eaten straight off the cob, at its best in mid to late summer.

observances.title: National Peanut Butter Cookie Day
observances.blurb: A day for the cookie; the crosshatch fork pattern became standard in recipes from the 1930s.

observances.title: National Sewing Machine Day
observances.blurb: A day for the invention that made mass-produced clothing possible in the 19th century.

observances.title: Flag Day
observances.blurb: Marks the adoption of the U.S. flag by the Continental Congress on June 14, 1777.

observances.title: National Smile Power Day
observances.blurb: An informal observance on the influence a friendly expression can have on others.

observances.title: National Fudge Day
observances.blurb: A day for the dense sugar candy, popular as a souvenir in U.S. tourist towns.

observances.title: National Apple Strudel Day
observances.blurb: A day for the Austrian pastry of thin stretched dough wrapped around spiced apples.

observances.title: National Go Fishing Day
observances.blurb: An informal prompt to spend time fishing, one of the most common outdoor pastimes in the U.S.

observances.title: Juneteenth
observances.blurb: Marks June 19, 1865, when enslaved people in Galveston, Texas were told of their freedom. A U.S. federal holiday since 2021.

observances.title: National Vanilla Milkshake Day
observances.blurb: A day for the blended drink; vanilla itself comes from the seed pod of a climbing orchid.

observances.title: National Selfie Day
observances.blurb: A day for the self-portrait photo, a term added to the Oxford dictionaries in 2013.

observances.title: National Onion Rings Day
observances.blurb: A day for the battered, deep-fried side dish.

observances.title: National Pink Day
observances.blurb: An informal day for the color, which only became strongly gendered in Western marketing in the 20th century.

observances.title: National Pralines Day
observances.blurb: A day for the confection; the New Orleans version uses pecans, cream, and brown sugar.

observances.title: National Catfish Day
observances.blurb: Established by presidential proclamation in 1987 to promote U.S. farm-raised catfish.

observances.title: National Beautician's Day
observances.blurb: A day to recognize hairdressers, barbers, and salon workers.

observances.title: National Sunglasses Day
observances.blurb: A day for eyewear that protects against UV light, promoted by a trade association for vision safety.

observances.title: National Ceviche Day
observances.blurb: A day for the Latin American dish of raw fish 'cooked' by the acid in citrus juice.

observances.title: National Almond Buttercrunch Day
observances.blurb: A day for the toffee candy studded with almonds.

observances.title: Social Media Day
observances.blurb: Started by Mashable in 2010 to mark the effect of social platforms on communication.

observances.title: National Flip Flop Day
observances.blurb: An informal summer observance for the sandal, promoted by a restaurant chain.

observances.title: Father's Day
observances.blurb: Honors fathers and fatherhood; the U.S. version, on the third Sunday in June, was first held in 1910 in Spokane, Washington.

observances.title: National Postal Worker Day
observances.blurb: A day to recognize the letter carriers and clerks who move the mail.

observances.title: World UFO Day
observances.blurb: Observed by enthusiasts on the anniversary of the 1947 Roswell incident.

observances.title: National Chocolate Wafer Day
observances.blurb: A day for the thin, crisp chocolate cookie, the base of many icebox cakes.

observances.title: Independence Day (USA)
observances.blurb: Marks the adoption of the Declaration of Independence on July 4, 1776. Traditionally observed with fireworks and cookouts.

observances.title: National Bikini Day
observances.blurb: Marks the July 5, 1946 debut of the modern two-piece swimsuit in Paris.

observances.title: National Fried Chicken Day
observances.blurb: A day for the dish, with deep roots in both Scottish frying methods and West African seasoning traditions in the American South.

observances.title: National Strawberry Sundae Day
observances.blurb: A day for the ice cream sundae topped with strawberry sauce.

observances.title: National Blueberry Day
observances.blurb: A day for the blueberry, one of the few widely eaten fruits native to North America.

observances.title: National Sugar Cookie Day
observances.blurb: A day for the simple cookie; a version is often traced to 18th-century German settlers in Nazareth, Pennsylvania.

observances.title: National Piña Colada Day
observances.blurb: A day for the rum, coconut, and pineapple cocktail, which originated in Puerto Rico.

observances.title: National Blueberry Muffin Day
observances.blurb: A day for the muffin; it is the official state muffin of Minnesota.

observances.title: National Pecan Pie Day
observances.blurb: A day for the Southern pie made with pecans, a nut native to the south-central U.S.

observances.title: National French Fry Day
observances.blurb: A day for fried potato strips; the dish likely originated in Belgium despite the name.

observances.title: National Mac and Cheese Day
observances.blurb: A day for baked macaroni and cheese; Thomas Jefferson helped popularize it in the U.S. after tasting it in Europe.

observances.title: National Gummi Worm Day
observances.blurb: A day for the candy, introduced by the German company Trolli in 1981.

observances.title: National Corn Fritters Day
observances.blurb: A day for the fried batter cake studded with corn kernels.

observances.title: World Emoji Day
observances.blurb: Held on July 17 because that is the date shown on the calendar emoji on Apple devices.

observances.title: National Caviar Day
observances.blurb: A day for salt-cured fish roe, traditionally from sturgeon in the Caspian and Black Seas.

observances.title: National Daiquiri Day
observances.blurb: A day for the rum, lime, and sugar cocktail, named after a beach near Santiago de Cuba.

observances.title: National Moon Day
observances.blurb: Marks July 20, 1969, when Apollo 11's crew made the first crewed landing on the Moon.

observances.title: National Junk Food Day
observances.blurb: An informal day to eat foods usually saved for occasional treats.

observances.title: National Mango Day
observances.blurb: A day for the mango, the most widely consumed fresh fruit in the world.

observances.title: National Vanilla Ice Cream Day
observances.blurb: A day for the most popular ice cream flavor in the U.S.

observances.title: National Drive-Thru Day
observances.blurb: Marks the mid-20th-century rise of drive-through service, which In-N-Out claims to have pioneered in 1948.

observances.title: National Hot Fudge Sundae Day
observances.blurb: A day for the sundae topped with warm chocolate sauce.

observances.title: National Bagelfest Day
observances.blurb: Tied to a bagel festival first held in Mattoon, Illinois, once home to a large bagel bakery.

observances.title: National Crème Brûlée Day
observances.blurb: A day for the custard dessert finished with a hard layer of caramelized sugar.

observances.title: National Milk Chocolate Day
observances.blurb: A day for milk chocolate, first made commercially viable by Daniel Peter and Henri Nestlé in the 1870s.

observances.title: National Lasagna Day
observances.blurb: A day for the layered baked pasta, one of the oldest recorded pasta dishes.

observances.title: International Day of Friendship
observances.blurb: A UN observance, established in 2011, promoting friendship between people, cultures, and countries.

observances.title: National Avocado Day
observances.blurb: A day for the avocado, a fruit cultivated in Mesoamerica for around 10,000 years.

observances.title: National Tequila Day
observances.blurb: A day for the agave spirit; true tequila can only be made in specific regions of Mexico.

observances.title: National Hot Dog Day
observances.blurb: A day for the sausage in a bun, promoted by the meat industry on the third Wednesday of July.

observances.title: National Raspberry Cream Pie Day
observances.blurb: A day for the pie combining tart raspberries with a sweet cream filling.

observances.title: National Ice Cream Sandwich Day
observances.blurb: A day for ice cream between two cookies or wafers, sold by New York street vendors as early as 1900.

observances.title: National Watermelon Day
observances.blurb: A day for the fruit, which is about 92% water and was cultivated in Africa thousands of years ago.

observances.title: National Chocolate Chip Cookie Day
observances.blurb: A day for the cookie invented by Ruth Wakefield at the Toll House Inn in Massachusetts around 1938.

observances.title: National Oyster Day
observances.blurb: A day for the shellfish, farmed and eaten since Roman times.

observances.title: National Root Beer Float Day
observances.blurb: A day for the drink of root beer and vanilla ice cream, said to date to 1893 in Colorado.

observances.title: National Lighthouse Day
observances.blurb: Marks the 1789 act of Congress that put lighthouses under federal control.

observances.title: National Frozen Custard Day
observances.blurb: A day for the dense dessert of ice cream made with egg yolks, strongly associated with the U.S. Midwest.

observances.title: Book Lovers Day
observances.blurb: An informal day to set aside time for reading.

observances.title: National S'mores Day
observances.blurb: A day for the campfire treat; the earliest known printed recipe appeared in a 1927 Girl Scouts handbook.

observances.title: National Raspberry Tart Day
observances.blurb: A day for the small open pastry filled with raspberries or raspberry jam.

observances.title: National Julienne Fries Day
observances.blurb: A day for thin-cut shoestring fries, named after the julienne knife technique.

observances.title: National Filet Mignon Day
observances.blurb: A day for the tender cut from the small end of the beef tenderloin.

observances.title: National Creamsicle Day
observances.blurb: A day for the frozen bar of vanilla ice cream in an orange sherbet shell.

observances.title: National Relaxation Day
observances.blurb: Created in 1985 by a then-nine-year-old as a day to deliberately do nothing productive.

observances.title: Tell a Joke Day
observances.blurb: An informal day for sharing jokes.

observances.title: National Thrift Shop Day
observances.blurb: A day for secondhand stores, many run by charities to fund social programs.

observances.title: National Fajita Day
observances.blurb: A day for the Tex-Mex dish of grilled strips of meat; the term comes from the Spanish for 'little belt.'

observances.title: National Potato Day
observances.blurb: A day for the potato, a staple crop domesticated in the Andes and now grown worldwide.

observances.title: National Chocolate Pecan Pie Day
observances.blurb: A day for pecan pie with chocolate added to the filling.

observances.title: National Senior Citizens Day
observances.blurb: Established by presidential proclamation in 1988 to recognize the contributions of older Americans.

observances.title: National Pecan Torte Day
observances.blurb: A day for the multi-layered nut cake.

observances.title: National Sponge Cake Day
observances.blurb: A day for one of the oldest non-yeast cakes, leavened by beaten eggs alone.

observances.title: National Waffle Day (USA)
observances.blurb: Marks the August 24, 1869 U.S. patent for a stovetop waffle iron.

observances.title: National Banana Split Day
observances.blurb: A day for the sundae, generally credited to a pharmacist in Latrobe, Pennsylvania in 1904.

observances.title: National Dog Day
observances.blurb: Founded in 2004 to celebrate dogs of all kinds and encourage adoption.

observances.title: National Pots de Crème Day
observances.blurb: A day for the loose French custard, served in small individual pots.

observances.title: National Cherry Turnover Day
observances.blurb: A day for the folded pastry filled with cherry preserves.

observances.title: National Lemon Juice Day
observances.blurb: A day for lemon juice, valued in cooking for its acidity and once carried on ships to prevent scurvy.

observances.title: National Toasted Marshmallow Day
observances.blurb: A day for marshmallows roasted over a fire; the modern candy descends from a French confection made with mallow root.

observances.title: National Trail Mix Day
observances.blurb: A day for the portable snack of nuts, dried fruit, and chocolate, popular with hikers.

observances.title: National Friendship Day
observances.blurb: Observed on the first Sunday in August in the U.S.; a broader International Day of Friendship falls on July 30.

observances.title: National Rum Day
observances.blurb: A day for rum, distilled from sugarcane byproducts and closely tied to Caribbean history.

observances.title: National No Rhyme (Nor Reason) Day
observances.blurb: An informal day noting English words with no perfect rhyme, such as 'orange' and 'silver.'

observances.title: National Blueberry Popsicle Day
observances.blurb: A day for the frozen fruit bar, near the end of the summer season.

observances.title: National Skyscraper Day
observances.blurb: Go outside and lean your head all the way back at something that shouldn't be able to stand up.

observances.title: National Wildlife Day
observances.blurb: Founded in 2005 to raise awareness of endangered species and the work of wildlife sanctuaries.

observances.title: National Cheese Pizza Day
observances.blurb: A day for the plain cheese pie, the baseline against which other pizzas are measured.

observances.title: Read a Book Day
observances.blurb: An informal prompt to start or finish a book.

observances.title: National Beer Lover's Day
observances.blurb: A day for beer, one of the oldest prepared drinks, with recipes recorded in ancient Mesopotamia.

observances.title: National Ampersand Day
observances.blurb: A day for the & symbol, a ligature of the Latin word 'et,' meaning 'and.'

observances.title: National Teddy Bear Day
observances.blurb: The stuffed bear is named after Theodore Roosevelt, who in 1902 refused to shoot a captured bear on a hunt.

observances.title: National TV Dinner Day
observances.blurb: A day for the frozen tray meal, mass-marketed by Swanson starting in 1953.

observances.title: Patriot Day

observances.title: National Chocolate Milkshake Day
observances.blurb: A day for the blended drink; the word 'milkshake' first appears in print in the 1880s.

observances.title: National Peanut Day
observances.blurb: A day for the peanut, a legume; George Washington Carver promoted its farming to restore Southern soil.

observances.title: National Cream-Filled Doughnut Day
observances.blurb: A day for filled doughnuts such as the Boston cream and the Bismarck.

observances.title: National Linguine Day
observances.blurb: A day for the flat, narrow pasta from the Liguria region of Italy.

observances.title: National Guacamole Day

observances.title: National Apple Dumpling Day

observances.title: National Cheeseburger Day
observances.blurb: A day for the cheeseburger; several 1920s diners claim to have added the first slice of cheese.

observances.title: Talk Like a Pirate Day
observances.blurb: Created by two friends in 1995 as an inside joke; it spread after a 2002 newspaper column.

observances.title: National Pepperoni Pizza Day
observances.blurb: A day for the most-ordered pizza topping in the U.S. Pepperoni is an American creation.

observances.title: International Day of Peace
observances.blurb: A UN observance since 1981, marked by a minute of silence at noon and calls for a global ceasefire.

observances.title: National Ice Cream Cone Day
observances.blurb: A day for the edible cone, widely popularized at the 1904 St. Louis World's Fair.

observances.title: National Great American Pot Pie Day
observances.blurb: A day for the savory pie of meat and vegetables in gravy under a crust.

observances.title: National Cherries Jubilee Day

observances.title: National Lobster Day

observances.title: National Pancake Day (USA)
observances.blurb: A day for pancakes, among the oldest cereal foods; the UK observes its own on Shrove Tuesday.

observances.title: National Chocolate Milk Day
observances.blurb: A day for the drink, credited to an Irish physician in Jamaica in the late 1600s.

observances.title: National Drink Beer Day
observances.blurb: An informal companion to Beer Lover's Day earlier in the month.

observances.title: National Coffee Day
observances.blurb: A day for coffee, first cultivated in Yemen and now one of the most traded commodities in the world.

observances.title: National Chewing Gum Day
observances.blurb: A day for gum; the modern chicle-based version was developed in the U.S. in the 1860s.

observances.title: Labor Day
observances.blurb: A U.S. federal holiday on the first Monday in September, honoring workers and the labor movement. First held in 1882.

observances.title: National Dance Day
observances.blurb: Founded in 2010 by dancer-choreographer Nigel Lythgoe to encourage people to be more active through dance.

observances.title: International Coffee Day
observances.blurb: Launched by the International Coffee Organization in 2015 to recognize coffee farmers and the trade.

observances.title: National Custodial Workers Day
observances.blurb: A day to recognize janitorial and cleaning staff.

observances.title: National Techies Day
observances.blurb: Created in 1999 to encourage young people toward careers in technology.

observances.title: National Taco Day
observances.blurb: A day for the taco; the word appears in Mexico in the 19th century, possibly from a mining term for a small charge.

observances.title: National Apple Betty Day
observances.blurb: A day for the baked dessert of spiced apples layered with buttered breadcrumbs, a colonial American dish.

observances.title: National Noodle Day
observances.blurb: A day for noodles; the oldest known example, found in China, is around 4,000 years old.

observances.title: National LED Light Day

observances.title: National Pierogi Day
observances.blurb: A day for the filled dumpling of Central and Eastern Europe, a staple of Polish-American communities.

observances.title: National Beer and Pizza Day
observances.blurb: An informal day for a common pairing.

observances.title: World Mental Health Day
observances.blurb: A WHO-recognized day, first held in 1992, to raise awareness and reduce stigma around mental illness.

observances.title: National Sausage Pizza Day
observances.blurb: A day for pizza topped with Italian sausage.

observances.title: National Gumbo Day

observances.title: National Yorkshire Pudding Day
observances.blurb: A UK day for the baked batter side dish traditionally served with roast beef.

observances.title: National Dessert Day
observances.blurb: A broad food holiday for sweet courses of all kinds.

observances.title: National Cheese Curd Day
observances.blurb: A day for fresh cheese curds, a Wisconsin staple; very fresh ones squeak against the teeth.

observances.title: World Food Day
observances.blurb: Marks the 1945 founding of the UN Food and Agriculture Organization; focused on hunger and food security.

observances.title: National Pasta Day
observances.blurb: A day for pasta, of which Italy recognizes hundreds of regional shapes.

observances.title: National Chocolate Cupcake Day
observances.blurb: A day for the single-serving cake; the term 'cupcake' appears in an American cookbook in 1828.

observances.title: National Seafood Bisque Day
observances.blurb: A day for the smooth, cream-based shellfish soup of French origin.

observances.title: National Chicken and Waffles Day
observances.blurb: A day for the dish, with roots in both Pennsylvania Dutch cooking and African-American cuisine in the South and Harlem.

observances.title: National Pumpkin Cheesecake Day
observances.blurb: A day for the autumn dessert combining cheesecake with spiced pumpkin.

observances.title: National Nut Day
observances.blurb: A broad day for edible nuts, a calorie-dense food source used since prehistory.

observances.title: National Boston Cream Pie Day
observances.blurb: A day for the dessert, which is actually a cake; it is the official state dessert of Massachusetts.

observances.title: United Nations Day
observances.blurb: Marks October 24, 1945, when the UN Charter entered into force.

observances.title: National Greasy Foods Day
observances.blurb: An informal day for fried and oil-rich foods.

observances.title: National Pumpkin Day
observances.blurb: A day for the pumpkin, a squash native to North America and central to autumn traditions.

observances.title: National American Beer Day
observances.blurb: A day for U.S. beer, from mass-market lagers to the craft breweries that number in the thousands.

observances.title: National Chocolate Day
observances.blurb: A day for chocolate, made from cacao seeds that Mesoamerican cultures once used as currency.

observances.title: National Cat Day
observances.blurb: Founded in 2005 to highlight cats in need of adoption.

observances.title: National Candy Corn Day
observances.blurb: A day for the tri-color candy, first made in the 1880s and originally called 'chicken feed.'

observances.title: Halloween
observances.blurb: Evolved from the Celtic festival of Samhain and the Christian Allhallowtide; now marked by costumes and trick-or-treating.

observances.title: National Boss's Day
observances.blurb: Registered in 1958 by a secretary who chose her father's birthday to honor supervisors.

observances.title: Indigenous Peoples' Day
observances.blurb: Observed the second Monday in October as an alternative to Columbus Day, honoring Native American peoples and history.

observances.title: National Vinegar Day
observances.blurb: A day for vinegar, used for food preservation and cleaning for thousands of years.

observances.title: National Deviled Egg Day
observances.blurb: A day for the stuffed halved egg; 'deviled' has referred to spiced foods since the 18th century.

observances.title: National Sandwich Day
observances.blurb: Marks the birthday of John Montagu, 4th Earl of Sandwich, after whom the food is named.

observances.title: National Candy Day
observances.blurb: A broad food holiday for sweets, conveniently placed just after Halloween.

observances.title: National Doughnut Appreciation Day
observances.blurb: Tied to the Salvation Army 'Doughnut Lassies' who served fried dough to U.S. soldiers in World War I.

observances.title: National Nachos Day
observances.blurb: A day for the dish, invented around 1940 by Ignacio 'Nacho' Anaya in Piedras Negras, Mexico.

observances.title: National Bittersweet Chocolate With Almonds Day
observances.blurb: An unusually specific food holiday for dark chocolate studded with almonds.

observances.title: National Cappuccino Day
observances.blurb: A day for the espresso drink; the name comes from the color of Capuchin friars' robes.

observances.title: National Scrapple Day

observances.title: National Vanilla Cupcake Day
observances.blurb: A day for the plain cupcake, the base for most decorated versions.

observances.title: Veterans Day

observances.title: National Pizza With the Works Except Anchovies Day
observances.blurb: One of the longest names on the food-holiday calendar, and a clear stance on toppings.

observances.title: World Kindness Day
observances.blurb: Introduced in 1998 by a coalition of humanitarian groups to promote kind acts across borders.

observances.title: National Pickle Day
observances.blurb: A day for pickled cucumbers; pickling as a preservation method is thousands of years old.

observances.title: National Clean Out Your Refrigerator Day
observances.blurb: Placed shortly before Thanksgiving, when U.S. kitchens need the space.

observances.title: National Fast Food Day
observances.blurb: A day marking the quick-service restaurant industry, which grew rapidly in the postwar U.S.

observances.title: National Baklava Day
observances.blurb: A day for the layered phyllo-and-nut pastry associated with the former Ottoman regions.

observances.title: National Vichyssoise Day
observances.blurb: A day for the chilled potato-and-leek soup, created at a New York hotel in the early 1900s.

observances.title: National Carbonated Beverage With Caffeine Day
observances.blurb: A precisely worded food holiday for what most people simply call soda or pop.

observances.title: National Peanut Butter Fudge Day
observances.blurb: A day for the softer, peanut-butter-based version of fudge.

observances.title: World Hello Day
observances.blurb: Begun in 1973 in response to conflict in the Middle East, promoting communication over force. Participants greet ten people.

observances.title: National Cranberry Relish Day
observances.blurb: Placed near Thanksgiving; cranberries are one of the few commercially grown fruits native to North America.

observances.title: National Espresso Day
observances.blurb: A day for espresso; the first patents for machines to make it date to early 1900s Italy.

observances.title: National Sardines Day
observances.blurb: A day for the small oily fish, named after the island of Sardinia.

observances.title: National Parfait Day
observances.blurb: A day for the layered dessert; 'parfait' is French for 'perfect.'

observances.title: National Cake Day
observances.blurb: A broad food holiday for cake, one of the oldest baked sweets.

observances.title: National Bavarian Cream Pie Day
observances.blurb: A day for pie filled with Bavarian cream, a custard set with gelatin and folded with whipped cream.

observances.title: National French Toast Day

observances.title: National Lemon Cream Pie Day
observances.blurb: A day for the pie of lemon custard under whipped cream, a lighter cousin of lemon meringue.

observances.title: National Mason Jar Day
observances.blurb: Marks the 1858 patent by John Landis Mason for the screw-top glass canning jar.

observances.title: Thanksgiving (USA)
observances.blurb: A U.S. federal holiday on the fourth Thursday in November, centered on a large meal and giving thanks. Made an annual national holiday in 1863.

observances.title: National Button Day
observances.blurb: Established in 1938 by the National Button Society for collectors of decorative buttons.

observances.title: National Eat a Red Apple Day
observances.blurb: An informal food holiday nodding to the saying about an apple a day.

observances.title: National Fritters Day
observances.blurb: A day for fritters: pieces of food or batter fried in fat, found in cuisines worldwide.

observances.title: National Roof Over Your Head Day
observances.blurb: An informal observance encouraging gratitude for shelter, especially in winter.

observances.title: National Cookie Day
observances.blurb: A day for cookies; the word comes from the Dutch 'koekje,' meaning little cake.

observances.title: National Sachertorte Day
observances.blurb: A day for the Viennese chocolate cake with apricot jam, created in 1832 for a Habsburg prince.

observances.title: National Gazpacho Day
observances.blurb: A day for the cold Spanish tomato-and-vegetable soup, from the Andalusia region.

observances.title: National Cotton Candy Day
observances.blurb: A day for spun sugar; the machine that made it a fairground staple was patented by a dentist in 1897.

observances.title: National Brownie Day
observances.blurb: A day for the chocolate bar cookie; an early recipe appeared in a 1906 Boston cookbook.

observances.title: National Pastry Day
observances.blurb: A broad day for baked goods made with enriched or laminated dough.

observances.title: National Lager Day

observances.title: National Noodle Ring Day
observances.blurb: A day for the baked noodle casserole set in a ring mold, a mid-century American dish.

observances.title: National Ambrosia Day
observances.blurb: A day for the Southern U.S. dish of oranges, coconut, and marshmallows, served as a salad or dessert.

observances.title: National Cocoa Day
observances.blurb: A day for hot cocoa, distinct from hot chocolate in using cocoa powder rather than melted chocolate.

observances.title: National Bouillabaisse Day
observances.blurb: A day for the Provençal fish stew from the port city of Marseille.

observances.title: National Cupcake Day
observances.blurb: A day for the individual cake; specialty cupcake shops surged in the 2000s.

observances.title: National Chocolate-Covered Anything Day
observances.blurb: Pretzels, strawberries, bacon, more chocolate. Dealer's choice.

observances.title: National Maple Syrup Day
observances.blurb: A day for maple syrup; it takes roughly 40 gallons of sap to make one gallon of syrup.

observances.title: National Roast Suckling Pig Day
observances.blurb: A day for the whole-roasted young pig, a festive centerpiece in many cultures.

observances.title: National Hard Candy Day
observances.blurb: A day for boiled sugar candy, one of the oldest confection types.

observances.title: National Sangria Day
observances.blurb: A day for the Spanish and Portuguese punch of wine, fruit, and sweetener.

observances.title: National Crossword Puzzle Day
observances.blurb: Marks December 21, 1913, when the first known crossword ran in the New York World.

observances.title: National Cookie Exchange Day
observances.blurb: A day for the holiday tradition where guests each bring a batch of cookies to swap.

observances.title: Festivus
observances.blurb: A secular anti-commercial holiday popularized by a 1997 episode of Seinfeld, including the 'airing of grievances.'

observances.title: Christmas Eve
observances.blurb: The evening before Christmas Day, marked by church services, family gatherings, and gift-giving in many countries.

observances.title: Christmas Day
observances.blurb: The Christian feast of the birth of Jesus, and a widely observed secular holiday. A public holiday in most countries.

observances.title: National Candy Cane Day
observances.blurb: A day for the striped peppermint stick, a Christmas confection since at least the 1600s in Europe.

observances.title: National Fruitcake Day
observances.blurb: A day for the dense cake of dried fruit and nuts, known for a very long shelf life.

observances.title: National Card Playing Day
observances.blurb: An informal day for card games during the quiet stretch between Christmas and New Year's.

observances.title: National Pepper Pot Day
observances.blurb: Tied to a peppery tripe soup said to have been served to Continental Army troops at Valley Forge in 1777.

observances.title: National Bicarbonate of Soda Day
observances.blurb: A day for baking soda, used in baking, cleaning, and deodorizing.

observances.title: New Year's Eve
observances.blurb: The last day of the year, marked by countdowns, fireworks, and gatherings in much of the world.

observances.title: National Champagne Day
observances.blurb: A day for the sparkling wine from the Champagne region of France, traditionally opened at midnight on New Year's Eve.

observances.title: National Ugly Sweater Day
observances.blurb: Observed the third Friday in December; ugly Christmas sweater parties took off in the 2000s.

observances.title: National Regifting Day
observances.blurb: Coined by a TV network in 2005 for the office-party habit of passing along unwanted gifts.

observances.title: National Irish Coffee Day
observances.blurb: Hot coffee, whiskey, sugar, and a collar of cream that floats if you pour it over a spoon.

observances.title: National Blueberry Pancake Day
observances.blurb: A food holiday for pancakes made with blueberries, a fruit native to North America.

observances.title: National Cook a Sweet Potato Day
observances.blurb: Roast it, mash it, or cut it into fries. Hard to get this one wrong.

observances.title: World Wildlife Day
observances.blurb: A UN observance, adopted in 2013, marking the 1973 signing of the treaty regulating trade in endangered species.

observances.title: National Black Forest Cake Day
observances.blurb: A day for the German layered cake of chocolate sponge, cherries, and kirsch, named after a mountain region.

observances.title: National Laundry Day
observances.blurb: The one chore that is never, at any point, fully done.

observances.title: National Eggs Benedict Day
observances.blurb: Poached eggs, ham, and hollandaise on a toasted English muffin. Brunch's flagship order.

observances.title: National Butterscotch Brownie Day
observances.blurb: The blondie: brown sugar and vanilla where a brownie would put cocoa.

observances.title: National I Love Reese's Day
observances.blurb: The peanut butter cup started as a one-man mail-order operation in the 1920s.

observances.title: National Tap Dance Day

observances.title: National Kitten Day
observances.blurb: A day to highlight kittens in shelters and the responsibilities of adopting one.

observances.title: National Raspberry Cake Day
observances.blurb: A food holiday for cakes made or filled with raspberries.

observances.title: National Roller Coaster Day

observances.title: National Cherry Popover Day

observances.title: National Salami Day
observances.blurb: A day for cured, seasoned sausage; the name comes from the Italian 'salare,' to salt.

observances.title: National Star Trek Day
observances.blurb: The original series first aired on September 8, 1966, and only lasted three seasons.

observances.title: National Butterscotch Pudding Day
observances.blurb: A day for the pudding flavored with brown sugar and butter, the defining notes of butterscotch.

observances.title: National Strawberry Cream Pie Day
observances.blurb: Fresh strawberries folded into whipped cream on a cookie crust. No oven required.

observances.title: National Moldy Cheese Day
observances.blurb: For blue, brie, and every cheese where the mold is the entire point.

observances.title: World Pasta Day
observances.blurb: Established at a 1995 pasta industry congress in Rome; distinct from the U.S. National Pasta Day on October 17.

observances.title: National Black Cat Day
observances.blurb: A UK awareness day, begun in 2011, noting that black cats are adopted from shelters less often than others.

observances.title: National Chicken Soup for the Soul Day
observances.blurb: An informal day tied to the inspirational book series, and to the long-standing use of chicken soup as comfort food.

observances.title: National Bundt Day
observances.blurb: The hole in the middle isn't decoration; it helps a heavy batter bake all the way through.

observances.title: National Play Monopoly Day
observances.blurb: Clear an afternoon, pick your token, and prepare to fall out with someone over Boardwalk.

observances.title: Dewey Decimal System Day
observances.blurb: The library scheme that files every subject in existence somewhere between 000 and 999.

observances.title: National Go Caroling Day
observances.blurb: A day for the tradition of singing carols door to door, which descends from medieval wassailing.

observances.title: National Visit the Zoo Day
observances.blurb: An informal day encouraging a trip to a local zoo or aquarium during the winter break.
